label: first copy step after outputting orig(0), in long (L=9) sequences
explanation: Copy-phase only (never original or delimiter steps). 90% of mass is at recall_idx==1 (step L+1, input = the echoed first token, output = orig(1)); the rest is at recall_idx==2. Strongly length-dependent: 81% of mass at L=9, 16% at L=8, little at L=7 and none at L<=5; firing rate at recall_idx 1 is ~49% for L=9. Magnitude also depends on the first token: a gives the strongest activations (all top examples start with a), then p, k, l, j, n, r, i. Digits and many letters (w, e, c, h, y, 3) often fail to fire. Looks like a position/length timer for the second output step of long sequences, gated by first-token identity. Restricting to a token set raises precision to ~0.65 but loses recall, so token gating is incomplete.
